questions.question: How can you lower the risk of a rollover?

options.text: Load cargo as far forward as possible.
Load cargo as far back as possible.
Load cargo as low as possible.
Stack cargo as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load cargo as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Load your cargo as close to the ground as possible to reduce rollover risk. Also take curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: What should you do if your trailer begins to skid?

options.text: Release the brakes.
Accelerate.
Turn the steering wheel quickly side to side.
Brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brakes.
questions.explanation: Release the brakes to help the wheels grip the road again. Once the wheels have traction, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic with a combination vehicle, what is most important?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for you.
Wait for other drivers to wave you in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. You must have a large enough gap in traffic before entering or crossing.

questions.question: What does a shut-off valve do?

options.text: It is located on the front of a trailer.
It is located on the instrument panel.
It stops air from escaping the brake system.
It should always be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops air from escaping the brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve must always be closed to keep air in the braking system.

questions.question: How can you best tell that your trailer is skidding?

options.text: By looking at other drivers' faces.
By seeing it in your mirrors.
By feeling it.
By listening to the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: By seeing it in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors. You will see the trailer move off course. This is the earliest and best way to spot a skid.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?

options.text: The signal line
The cable line
The surplus line
The power line

questions.correctAnswerText: The signal line
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the signal line or control line.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?

options.text: The control line
The utility line
The open line
The parallel line

questions.correctAnswerText: The control line
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line or signal line.

questions.question: Which shut-off valves should be open during a trip?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
The rear shut-off valves should be open.
All valves should be open except the rear shut-off valves.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All valves should be open except the rear shut-off valves.
questions.explanation: Keep all shut-off valves open except the ones at the very back. This ensures air reaches all trailer brakes and does not escape from the rear of your vehicle.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, what should the trailer height be?

options.text: Slightly higher than the center of the fifth wheel.
Level with the center of the fifth wheel.
Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
Next to the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: The trailer should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel when connecting the converter dolly.

questions.question: What can happen if you do not keep the fifth wheel plate greased?

options.text: The trailer could disconnect.
Steering problems could occur.
Braking problems could occur.
The lights could be affected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering problems could occur.
questions.explanation: Without proper lubrication on the fifth wheel plate, friction builds up between the tractor and trailer, causing steering problems.

questions.question: Trailers with low underneath clearance may be difficult to drive:

options.text: On interstate highways.
Over railroad crossings.
On dirt roads.
At the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings can be hard to cross with a low-clearance trailer. Long trailers and single-axle tractors have extra trouble crossing raised railroad tracks.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer:

options.text: Make sure to couple matching glad hands.
Any glad hand can be connected to any other glad hand.
It is best to leave one glad hand unattached.
Only one set of glad hands should be connected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure to couple matching glad hands.
questions.explanation: When coupling, connect matching glad hands. They are color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: When driving a bobtail tractor, you should be aware that:

options.text: Bobtails stop very easily.
Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with semitrailers.
Bobtails are more difficult to stop than tractors with semitrailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails are more difficult to stop than tractors with semitrailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor with no trailer attached. When driving a bobtail, stopping is harder and takes longer than stopping a tractor with a loaded trailer.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

questions.correctAnswerText: Two
questions.explanation: All combination vehicles have two air lines: the service line and the emergency line.

questions.question: After connecting the air lines to the trailer while coupling, you should:

options.text: Supply air to the trailer.
Chock the wheels.
Inspect the fifth wheel.
Connect the electrical cord.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supply air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Following the coupling steps in the right order is important for safe operation. After connecting the air lines to the trailer, supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination:

options.text: Cargo weight must be evenly distributed between all trailers.
The heaviest trailer should be positioned directly behind the cab.
The heaviest trailer should be positioned in the rear.
The weight of the trailers does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: The heaviest trailer should be positioned directly behind the cab.
questions.explanation: Place the heaviest loaded trailer closest to the tractor. Place the lightest trailer in the rear.

questions.question: What does the tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Protects the tractor from being stolen
Protects the tractor from exceeding a set speed
Keeps air in the braking system, should the trailer break away or develop a leak
Ensures oil adequately lubricates the engine

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the braking system, should the trailer break away or develop a leak
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor braking system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: If a load is placed on one side of a trailer, the trailer:

options.text: May lean, and could result in a rollover.
May add extra support during turns.
Have improved braking.
Have improved steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: May lean, and could result in a rollover.
questions.explanation: If a load is placed mainly on one side of a trailer, the trailer may lean to one side and could roll over.

questions.question: Before a drive, ensure that air flows to all trailers by:

options.text: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air.
Closing the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air.
Disconnecting air supply lines and listening for escaping air.
Rolling each trailer down a hill and testing the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that air reaches all trailers. Wait for air pressure to build, then send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, air is reaching the entire vehicle.

questions.question: When driving a combination rig, following distance should be:

options.text: Decreased in poor weather.
Shorter than when driving a single vehicle.
About the same as when driving a single vehicle.
Longer than when driving a single vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Longer than when driving a single vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep a longer following distance when driving a combination rig than when driving a single vehicle. Combinations need more distance to stop.
